query: For phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys, what single intervention could improve glass-forming ability and the thermal stability of the amorphous state? Formulate one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention without presupposing its class, the mechanism by which it would act, the predicted improvement relative to an otherwise comparable baseline, the conditions under which it should or should not work, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of phosphorus to high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys can improve glass-forming ability and thermal stability of the amorphous state.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy or compositionally complex alloys in their crystalline state
generation.conditions: Alloy composition, cooling rate, and phosphorus content
generation.structural_mediator: Phosphorus-induced changes in alloy structure and bonding
generation.mechanism: Phosphorus atoms may occupy interstitial sites, altering the alloy's lattice structure and enhancing glass-forming ability
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved glass-forming ability and thermal stability of the amorphous state
generation.baseline: High-entropy or compositionally complex alloys without phosphorus addition
generation.boundary: Phosphorus content, alloy composition, and processing conditions
generation.uncertainty: Optimal phosphorus content, effects of phosphorus on alloy microstructure, and potential interactions with other alloying elements

falsification_experiment.design: Comparative study of high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys with and without phosphorus addition
measurements: Thermal stability of the amorphous state
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of phosphorus does not improve glass-forming ability and thermal stability of the amorphous state, the hypothesis is falsified.
